audit.whatIsWrong: Level 2 was scored Skill while whys[1] says 'He keeps the range edge and can free-hit your low-HP Powder Keg'. Levels 3, 4-5 and 2+ items were scored Gangplank while whys[2] ends 'so it evens out', whys[3] ends 'neither side takes over the lane', and whys[6] ends 'so it stays even'. Level 6 was scored Ziggs while whys[4] ends 'keeping it down to skill'.
audit.why: 48.89% over 452 games in a poke lane that never really breaks: he owns the first two levels, the middle is even, your only owned stage is the Sheen item. The packet chart (Ziggs, Ziggs, Skill, Skill, Skill, Gangplank, Skill) matches the prose on every row.
audit.corrected: Both layers set to the packet chart, ratings rescaled.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4] and phases[6] were the stock 'Cannon Barrage wins fights you are not even in' and 'your pattern is at full power' lines.
audit.why: The real level-6 shape is that Cannon Barrage punishes a champion with no dash, but Satchel Charge knocks you out of the dive on a 20s cooldown at rank 1; the real late-game shape is that you both scale and neither closes. The full layer said neither.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer never states the range gap that defines the lane (Bouncing Bomb 850 versus Parrrley 625, and it bounces over the wave), never states that Satchel Charge deals percent-max-health damage, and dosFull[2]'s detail is a trading line under a title about Q-poking gold.
audit.why: The percent-health flag on Satchel Charge is the reason 'build resistances' is the wrong instinct here, and the range gap is the reason you cannot trade back before your second E point. The content layer knows about the range gap; the full layer does not.
audit.corrected: Range gap into phases[0].why, percent-health into dontsFull[2].d, and the correct cleanse scope into dosFull[2].d.

audit.why: The content layer already carries the sharpest fact in this matchup and states it twice: Remove Scurvy cleanses Hexplosive Minefield's slow but will NOT save you from Satchel Charge's knockback. That is exactly the kind of distinction the audit is looking for and it did not need touching — I only mirrored it into the full layer's do's.

edits.before: Q-poke costs him HP and pays you gold. Identify how Ziggs contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Bouncing Bomb reaches 850 to your Parrrley's 625 and bounces over the wave — you cannot trade back yet.

edits.before: First barrel chains start zoning his wave positions. Only take the trade when Ziggs's Satchel Charge is down.
edits.after: Still his: he holds the range edge and one auto or stray bomb kills a fresh keg before it ever arms.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Ziggs must walk into your range.
edits.after: Second E point lets you set a keg, step back and Parrrley-detonate from range — the lane evens out here.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Satchel Charge's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: You stabilise on keg poke and the W cleanse-heal, but his 850 bomb still matches your detonation reach, so neither side takes over.

edits.before: Cannon Barrage wins fights you are not even in — watch the map. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Ziggs's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Even at 6: Cannon Barrage punishes a dash-less Ziggs, but Satchel Charge knocks you back out of the dive. Bait the 20s W first.

edits.before: Two items on: your pattern is at full power. Ziggs carry threat 7.5/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: You both scale: your keg chain one-shots any slip, but his minefield and bombs still zone you out on even items.

edits.before: Chain a barrel behind the wave, Q-pop it as Ziggs steps to farm, and orange away whatever he answers with.
edits.after: Set a keg behind the wave, step back, and Parrrley-detonate from range so you never eat a bomb to trade.

edits.before: Letting him pop your barrels for free — every broken keg is gold and tempo handed across the lane.
edits.after: Walking up to place or hit a keg with Satchel Charge up — he knocks you out of your own detonation.

edits.before: His knockback + self-peel escape. Engage when it's down. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: 20s at rank 1 and it knocks you back out of the fight — bait it before you commit a chain.

edits.before: Ziggs wastes Satchel Charge — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Remove Scurvy cleanses his minefield slow, never the W knockback.

edits.before: That is Ziggs's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: A fresh keg dies to one auto or a stray Bouncing Bomb before it arms.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Hold W for the minefield slow and the heal, not as a panic button.

edits.before: Letting him pop your barrels for free — every broken keg is gold and tempo handed across the lane.
edits.after: Satchel Charge deals percent max health and knocks you away, so armour is not the save.

notes: Both packet suspect names ('Powder Kegs', 'Save Satchel Charge') are false positives. Not asserted anywhere: whether Satchel Charge's self-knockback can be used to escape a Cannon Barrage zone or whether Hexplosive Minefield's mines destroy Powder Kegs on contact — neither is answerable from Riot's text, and the second one in particular would materially change the wave-management advice if true.
